relevance.rationale: Genuine orphan with two named places that want it. First, conj:three-knot-jet-order-independence states that the Habiro cyclotomic expansion J_K(q) = sum c_n(K) (q;q)_n supplies the vertical jet-degree grading and that algebraic independence to order N is 'strictly decidable' — but it is stated for three knots. This document gives explicit q-hypergeometric formulas for the colored Jones polynomial of the double twist knots K(-m,-p) and K(-m,p), i.e. computable c_n for an infinite family, which is exactly the data needed to test that decidable claim beyond three knots. Second, conj:b1-hyperbolic-rows-theorem conditionally covers twist-knot rows and its Table 2 lists Bring-embeddable hyperbolic knots awaiting Volume-Conjecture discharge; twist knots are the p = 1 sub-family here. Honest scope: this paper supplies FORMULAS, not VC discharges, so it does not close any Table 2 row — the corpus's own text says 'the rate-limiting step is the VC discharge per knot', and this is not one. I read the abstract, §1 and eq. (1.1) (the Lauridsen cyclotomic expansion the paper builds on). Supporting, not core: no folio block currently uses double-twist-knot cyclotomic coefficients.

keyResults.statement: Explicit formulas for the colored Jones polynomial of the double twist knots K(-m,-p) and K(-m,p), which in the (-m,-p) case yield q-hypergeometric families generalizing the Kontsevich-Zagier series, together with a duality at roots of unity with the generating function for strongly unimodal sequences.
keyResults.useForFolio: Supplies computable cyclotomic coefficients c_n(K) for an infinite knot family, which is the input conj:three-knot-jet-order-independence needs to be tested past its current three knots.

proposedActions.rationale: No ref() entry; two blocks (the jet-order-independence conjecture and the hyperbolic-rows conjecture) work with exactly the objects this paper computes.

The folio computes Habiro cyclotomic expansions for the Borromean rings (computations/habiro_borromean_colored_jones.py, aj_borromean_colored_jones_tower.py). The double-twist formulas here are an independent source of c_n for a family that includes 4_1 (= K(2)), giving a cross-check of the folio's cyclotomic machinery on a knot it already uses. Cross-check only — do not adopt any coefficient because it matches.

relevance.rationale: Proves a formula for the colored Jones polynomial of the double twist knots K(-m,-p) and K(-m,p); in the (-m,-p) case this produces new families of q-hypergeometric series generalising the Kontsevich-Zagier series, and comparison with the cyclotomic expansion of the K(m,p) colored Jones gives a generalisation of the root-of-unity duality between the Kontsevich-Zagier function and the generating function for strongly unimodal sequences. The corpus's Habiro layer sits inside this family: prop:habiro-tail-archimedean-action works with the 4_1 Kashaev-Habiro cyclotomic tail S(q) = sum prod (1-q^j)(1-q^{-j}) and its resurgent action pi^2/5, masbaum2003 is registered specifically for Habiro's TWIST-knot cyclotomic expansions (4_1 = K_{-1}, trefoil = K_1), and the document itself notes that its m = 1 specialisation K(1,p) is the usual p-th twist knot. So this is the one-parameter generalisation of the exact family the corpus computes in, and the strongly-unimodal duality is the kind of q-series identity the c_k / Habiro programme keeps looking for. Supporting rather than core: the corpus's derivations all live at 4_1 and the trefoil, which are already covered by the registered twist-knot source; nothing here is consumed today, and the value is as a family to cross-check against.

keyResults.statement: An explicit formula for the colored Jones polynomial of the double twist knots K(-m,-p) and K(-m,p), yielding new q-hypergeometric families generalising the Kontsevich-Zagier series, with m = 1 recovering the usual twist knots.
keyResults.useForFolio: Extends the corpus's single-knot Habiro-tail computation to a two-parameter family, giving cross-check targets for the tail's bar-parity and resurgent-action machinery beyond 4_1.
